input:
/data/legacy holds text files in mixed encodings. For every file whose name ends in `.txt` (case-sensitive), write a normalised copy with the same name to /out/clean/: UTF-8 without BOM, line endings 
 and lone  converted to 
, and ending with exactly one added 
 if the text did not already end with 
.
Detect each file's encoding in this order: starts with a UTF-16 BOM (FF FE or FE FF) -> utf-16; starts with the UTF-8 BOM -> utf-8-sig; decodes as UTF-8 -> utf-8 (plain ASCII included); otherwise latin-1.
Write /out/manifest.tsv (tab-separated, header name, encoding, lines, chars) with one row per file sorted by name, where lines is the number of 
 and chars the number of Unicode characters in the normalised text (newlines included, BOM excluded).

transcript.final_response: Created normalized UTF-8 copies of all six `.txt` files in `/out/clean/` and wrote the sorted `/out/manifest.tsv`.
tool_calls: find /data/legacy -type f -name '*.txt' -print 2>/dev/null | sort; printf '\n'; ls -la /data/legacy 2>/dev/null; ls -la /out 2>/dev/null

mkdir -p /out/clean && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import csv
src = Path('/data/legacy')
out = Path('/out/clean')
rows = []
for path in sorted((p for p in src.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.name.endswith('.txt')), key=lambda p: p.name):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    if raw.startswith((b'\xff\xfe', b'\xfe\xff')):
        encoding = 'utf-16'
    elif raw.startswith(b'\xef\xbb\xbf'):
        encoding = 'utf-8-sig'
    else:
        try:
            raw.decode('utf-8')
            encoding = 'utf-8'
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            encoding = 'latin-1'
    text = raw.decode(encoding)
    text = text.replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '\n')
    if not text.endswith('\n'):
        text += '\n'
    (out / path.name).write_bytes(text.encode('utf-8'))
    rows.append((path.name, encoding, text.count('\n'), len(text)))
with (Path('/out') / 'manifest.tsv').open('w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter='\t', lineterminator='\n')
    writer.writerow(('name', 'encoding', 'lines', 'chars'))
    writer.writerows(rows)
PY
cat /out/manifest.tsv
for f in /out/clean/*.txt; do printf '%s ' "$f"; file "$f" 2>/dev/null; done
